_note: FOREGROUND PRESENTATION (parity/F02-notifications.md §3a `presentation`, and the claimable `notify.received` hook). THE DEFAULT IS NOTHING, on every platform, and it surprises every author: a push that arrives while the app is open shows no banner, plays no sound and appears in no list unless the app says otherwise. iOS makes it a delegate callback nobody implements; Android makes it a channel-importance question; the browser shows the notification but the page usually never hears about it. One word, `presentation({ foreground: [...] })`, decides it everywhere, and this corpus is the fold.
_note_words: The four words, canonical order. `banner` is an accepted alias of `alert` because that is what the platform calls it in its own settings UI; anything else is a refusal, never a silent drop.

fold.name: THE DEFAULT: nothing is presented while the app is open
iOS presents exactly what was configured, in canonical order
banner is an accepted spelling of alert and folds to it exactly once
A CLAIMED notify.received SUPPRESSES THE SYSTEM PRESENTATION, whatever was configured
a claim suppresses on Android too, where the OS would otherwise post regardless
ANDROID ALWAYS PUTS IT IN THE SHADE: `list` is implicit and cannot be configured away
Android: a heads-up needs BOTH the alert word and a high-importance channel
Android: alert on a LOW channel is DEGRADED and reported, because the channel wins and the app cannot override it
Android: a max-importance channel heads up
Web: there is no notification list to land in, so `list` is dropped and said so
Web: badge rides the Badging API and survives
a word that is not a presentation option is refused rather than ignored
